# Appendix A: Data Description {.unnumbered}

## A.1 Data Sources

The analysis uses three primary data sources. First, HUD Disaster Recovery Grant Reporting (DRGR) system quarterly performance reports (QPR) provide activity-level financial data on CDBG-DR programs spanning disasters from 2003 through 2023. Second, Bureau of Labor Statistics Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW) data for NAICS 925110 (Administration of Housing Programs) provide staffing and payroll proxies for administrative capacity. Third, CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) data provide contextual vulnerability indicators. U.S. Census Bureau geography files (2023 vintage county and state shapefiles) provide the spatial matching backbone.

## A.2 Data Flow

@tbl-data-flow summarizes the pipeline from raw administrative records to the 573-jurisdiction SEM sample.

| Stage | Count | Description |
|---|---:|---|
| Standardized DRGR/QPR activity-quarter rows | 130,605 | Repository-standardized administrative rows |
| Rows with valid actual-quarter labels | 128,382 | Excludes rows with missing QPR Actual Quarter |
| Collapsed grantee-disaster-quarter rows | 3,623 | Quarter-collapsed standardized panel |
| Recovered archived jurisdiction profiles | 577 | Raw bundled CSV before exclusions |
| Reference complete-case SEM sample | 573 | 30 state agencies + 543 county-linked local jurisdictions |

: Data flow from raw QPR to analytic sample {#tbl-data-flow}

The four excluded profiles are grantees with missing values on one or more SEM indicators after z-score standardization. The 573-jurisdiction sample represents all administering jurisdictions with complete data on the 10 SEM indicator variables and 6 covariates.

## A.3 Variable Dictionary

@tbl-variables defines all variables used in the SEM.

| Variable | Construction | Source | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| avg_employment | Mean QCEW annual employment, NAICS 925110 | BLS QCEW | Higher = more staff |
| avg_payroll | Mean QCEW annual payroll, NAICS 925110 | BLS QCEW | Higher = more payroll |
| programs_per_staff | Num_Program / (avg_employment $\times$ E_TOTPOP) | Derived | Higher = heavier workload |
| disasters_per_staff | Num_Disaster / (avg_employment $\times$ E_TOTPOP) | Derived | Higher = heavier workload |
| Ratio_disbursed_to_obligated | Cumulative disbursed / cumulative obligated | DRGR/QPR | Higher = better flow-through |
| Ratio_expended_to_disbursed | Cumulative expended / cumulative disbursed | DRGR/QPR | Higher = better utilization |
| Ratio_obligated_funds_fully_expended | Share of obligated funds reaching full expenditure | DRGR/QPR | Higher = more completion |
| Ratio_Program_Completed | Share of programs reaching completion | DRGR/QPR | Higher = more completion |
| Duration_of_completion | Months from first obligation to 95% expenditure | DRGR/QPR | Higher = slower |
| Average_Duration_Program_Completion | Mean program-level completion duration | DRGR/QPR | Higher = slower |
| state_level | Binary: 1 = state agency, 0 = local jurisdiction | Derived | --- |
| E_TOTPOP | Census total population (in thousands) | Census | --- |
| SPL_THEME1 | SVI: Socioeconomic vulnerability | CDC/ATSDR | Higher = more vulnerable |
| SPL_THEME2 | SVI: Household composition and disability | CDC/ATSDR | Higher = more vulnerable |
| SPL_THEME3 | SVI: Minority status and language | CDC/ATSDR | Higher = more vulnerable |
| SPL_THEME4 | SVI: Housing type and transportation | CDC/ATSDR | Higher = more vulnerable |

: Variable definitions {#tbl-variables}

All continuous variables are z-scored before SEM estimation. The workload indicators (programs_per_staff, disasters_per_staff) and duration indicators are reverse-coded so that higher values on all SEM indicators point in the conceptually positive direction (more capacity, better performance, faster timeliness).

## A.4 QCEW Proxy Documentation

QCEW data are extracted for NAICS 925110 ("Administration of Housing Programs, Urban Planning, and Community Development") at the county and state levels. This is an indirect proxy for CDBG-DR administrative capacity: it captures employment and payroll in the broader housing-program administration sector, not disaster-recovery staff specifically. It omits contractors, temporary teams, interagency staffing, and disaster-specific surge capacity.

@tbl-proxy-distributions reports pre-standardization distributions by government type. The most important finding is that 85.1% of local jurisdictions report zero QCEW employment, likely reflecting BLS suppression of small-cell counts rather than a literal absence of housing-program staff. This floor-value concentration means the QCEW proxy carries meaningful variation only among the 15% of local jurisdictions with non-suppressed data and among state agencies (all of which report non-zero values).

| Variable | Group | N | Min | P25 | Median | P75 | Max | % Zero |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| avg_employment | All | 573 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 10.50 | 80.6% |
| avg_employment | State | 30 | 0.11 | 0.40 | 1.20 | 2.27 | 5.37 | 0.0% |
| avg_employment | Local | 543 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 10.50 | 85.1% |
| avg_payroll | All | 573 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 129,361 | 80.6% |
| avg_payroll | State | 30 | 2,692 | 6,591 | 21,950 | 29,861 | 112,612 | 0.0% |
| avg_payroll | Local | 543 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 129,361 | 85.1% |

: QCEW proxy distributions before standardization {#tbl-proxy-distributions}

**Zero-employment handling in burden indicators.** The workload-manageability ratios (programs_per_staff and disasters_per_staff) require dividing program and disaster counts by QCEW employment. Because 85.1% of local jurisdictions report zero QCEW employment, a small epsilon offset ($\epsilon$ = 10$^{-6}$) is added to the denominator before division to avoid computational infinity. For jurisdictions with zero QCEW employment, this offset means the workload indicators are effectively proportional to raw program and disaster counts rather than staffing-scaled ratios, because the epsilon denominator neutralizes the staffing component. After z-score standardization, these jurisdictions form a large cluster with similar extreme pre-standardized values, and the distribution of the burden indicators is dominated by the zero-employment majority. This computational treatment is a limitation: it means the workload indicators carry meaningfully different information for the approximately 20% of observations with non-zero QCEW employment (where the indicators reflect genuine staffing-workload ratios) versus the 80% with zero employment (where they reduce to scaled program counts). The sign reversal when raw portfolio counts replace staffing ratios (Appendix C.6) is partly a consequence of this distributional feature.

The temporal alignment of QCEW data relative to recovery outcomes is approximate: QCEW annual averages span the years in which each jurisdiction administered CDBG-DR grants, but they are not quarter-matched to the QPR reporting periods.

## A.5 SVI Vintage Specification

SVI data are drawn from the CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index. Because SVI percentile scores are not directly comparable across vintage releases (the underlying variable set and weighting scheme have changed), the analysis uses a single SVI vintage assigned to each jurisdiction based on the closest available release year to the midpoint of the jurisdiction's CDBG-DR administration period. The four theme-level summary scores (Socioeconomic, Household Composition/Disability, Minority Status/Language, Housing Type/Transportation) are used as covariates rather than the overall SVI composite.

## A.6 Geography Matching

Jurisdictions in the DRGR/QPR system are identified by grantee labels that do not always correspond to standard Census geographic units. The matching procedure uses a three-step hierarchy:

1. **State agencies**: Two-letter state abbreviations matched directly to the 2023 Census state file (STUSPS field). Result: 30/30 matched (100%) via official state abbreviation lookup.
2. **Local jurisdictions**: Organization names containing county, parish, or borough identifiers matched directly to the 2023 Census county file by normalized label and state. Result: 543/543 matched (100%) via official county name crosswalk.
3. **Unresolved cases**: 0 jurisdiction labels could not be resolved to an official Census GEOID.

County-linked local units inherit county-level GEOIDs; state-administered units inherit statewide GEOIDs. All 573 matches (30 state + 543 local) achieved 100% confidence through official Census name matching; no city-to-county inference or manual disambiguation was required for the final SEM sample. This reflects the relatively clean naming conventions in the DRGR system for jurisdictions with sufficient QPR data to appear in the analytic sample.

**Ecological slippage.** The county-linking strategy introduces an ecological assumption: county-level SVI and population covariates are assigned to the administering jurisdiction even when the administrative actor's service area does not precisely align with county boundaries. For state agencies, statewide covariates aggregate over highly heterogeneous sub-state conditions. For city-level entities linked to counties, the county-level covariates may not reflect the specific neighborhoods or populations served by the CDBG-DR program. This ecological slippage is a recognized limitation of the geography layer and may attenuate or distort associations between contextual covariates and recovery outcomes.
